nodes.intent: where the body lies and the party is hired
nodes.note: A low room with the bier already made up. Halda is at her brother's head and has been for a while.

stations.note: The trestles the bier stands on. The body's first mark, and the first cutscene subject.
Halda's station. She does not move until the bier does.

nodes.intent: the roofed gate where a procession rests the bier before the road
nodes.note: The one enclosed place on the route, which is why the eulogy is spoken here and not in the open.

stations.note: The gate stone. The bier stands on it through the eulogy sequence.

nodes.intent: the open carry, where the argument catches up with the procession
nodes.note: Straight, sea on one hand, nothing to look at. Long enough that the party is walking rather than arriving.

stations.note: Where the bearers change hands and Ceren steps up out of the field onto the road.

nodes.intent: where the road divides and the party decides
nodes.note: A clearing with a cut stone carrying both names. The whole delve is built to arrive here.

stations.note: The fork stone. The bier is set down beside it while the party chooses.
Wick waits here with his spade because nobody has told him which hole to finish.

nodes.intent: the level honour road the keepers are carried on
nodes.note: Dry, straight and easy. Choosing it costs the procession nothing, which is the point of offering it.

stations.note: A breath partway along, where the drowned lane is visible below and to the east.

nodes.intent: the sunken lane through the water the sluice made
nodes.note: It drops below the fields and the water stands in it. The bearers go in to the knee and come back up.

stations.note: The lowest point of the lane, where the water is deepest and the procession has to keep going.

nodes.intent: the shoulder below the barrow where both roads meet
nodes.note: Whichever way the bier came, it is set down here once before the last climb. Both endings are staged from this ground.

stations.note: The last rest. The two-shot of Halda and Ceren is framed here.

nodes.intent: the keepers' burial ground on the headland
nodes.note: Open to the sky and the sea, one grave already cut. Everything ends standing around it.

stations.note: The cut grave. Where the bier is laid down and the campaign ends.
